findings.F1: Across all 17,236 coin-days, the next day's return beyond the coin's normal drift falls as the day's own return rises (slope -0.064, t -2.96 with cases summed per day, 2,874 days), so daily moves partly reverse.
findings.F2: The reversal sits mainly on the side of falls: after the 10 % largest one-day falls (below -4.9 %), the next day ends +0.68 % above drift (t 2.42, 1,724 cases, 625 days); after the largest falls measured against 20-day volatility (z below -1.17), it ends +0.54 % above drift (t 1.97, 1,436 cases); after the largest rises it ends only -0.19 % (t -0.84).
findings.F3: Among those large-fall days, the rebound grows the nearer the day closes to its low: +1.26 % (t 2.97, 430 cases, 226 days) when the close sits in the bottom 9 % of the range, +0.75 % (t 1.90) and +0.78 % (t 1.85) in the next two quarters, and -0.03 % (t -0.05) when the close is more than 29 % off the low.
findings.F4: The large-fall rebound is positive on every coin (BTC +0.47 %, ETH +0.51 %, LTC +0.36 %, XMR +1.32 % with t 3.58, XRP +0.68 %, ZEC +0.74 % with t 2.09) and in every year from 2018 to 2025 (+0.00 % to +1.60 %), weakest in 2025.
findings.F5: The tested idea did not show: wide flat days after a 5-day fall were followed by +0.93 % above drift over 5 days (t 0.42, 34 cases), the step-5 size was -1.28 % (t -0.55), and the book had a Sharpe of -0.18 while in a position on only 3 % of coin-days.
findings.F6: Contrary to the brief, wide flat days after the strongest 5-day rises (+17 % or more) were followed by more rise, not less: +3.26 % above drift the next day (t 2.17, 27 cases) and +4.83 % over 5 days (t 1.62, 26 cases). With so few cases and so many angles examined, this cannot be told apart from chance.
findings.F7: Across the other angles examined (5-day z-score, range ratio, close location, signed body and 20-day return, each in five bins on the 5-day grid; volatility level; weekday), no bin reached |t| 2.1. The largest was Friday's next day at +0.30 % (t 2.09), which is not distinct from chance given the number of angles examined.

ideas.idea: On a day a coin falls sharply against its own 20-day daily volatility, the nearer its close lands to the day's low, the larger its rise over the next day.
ideas.consequence: A trader would buy a sharp down day that closes on its low, sized by how close the close is to the low, and would not buy one that has already bounced well off its low.
ideas.name: close-at-low fall rebounds

ideas.idea: The larger a coin's one-day fall measured in its 20-day daily volatility, the larger its rise over the next day.
ideas.consequence: A trader would lean long the day after a fall, in proportion to how unusual that fall was for the coin, and would hold for about a day.
ideas.name: sharp daily fall reverses
